title: Robustness beyond one synthetic world
summary: We re-ran AI-1 on five independently generated worlds and six shifted worlds, removed each scam family from training in turn, and tested QR Shield on a disguise it never saw.

headline.label: Scams caught at 5% alerts, 5 new worlds (mean)

sections.title: Five independently generated worlds (new seeds)
sections.lead: The deployed Phase-1 model, unchanged, on five new worlds of ~2.2 million events each; test = unseen customers.
sections.takeaway: Across 5 new worlds the unchanged model catches 82%-89% of scams at a 5% alert rate; the rule catches 17%-24%.

sections.title: Six distribution shifts (scam process changed, model NOT retrained)
sections.lead: Each world changes how scammers behave; we measure the deployed model before any retraining, then after retraining.
sections.takeaway: Robust to prevalence, amount and label-noise shifts; the hardest case (older bought mule accounts AND smaller amounts) lowers PR-AUC, still far above the rule, and the drop in conformal coverage is the drift signal that triggers retraining.

sections.title: Scam families the model never saw
sections.lead: Each scam family is removed from training in turn; recall on that family at the pause threshold.
sections.takeaway: Most new scam types are still caught because the receiving mule wallet behaves the same; 'investment group' (repeat payments into a group) generalises worst, which is why the Case Linker feedback loop exists.

sections.title: QR Shield: a disguise trick it never saw, and learning from analysts
sections.lead: Family D (rotating payer ring) was hidden from training. Analysts confirm a few D shops from the weekly review list; those become labels.

chart.x_label: analyst-confirmed examples of the new trick

sections.takeaway: With 0 examples D recall is 42%; with 10 confirmed examples it is 58% and precision stays 92.5%.

caveats: All worlds come from our simulator; independent worlds and shifts test robustness, not real-world accuracy.
Retraining on shifted worlds uses the Phase-1 protocol with a fixed number of trees (no new cross-validation).
